text:
customer-alicia: Hey team — trying to finish the on‑prem POC. Logs aren't showing up in our Splunk HEC forwarder and traces in the console lack trace_id. Also saw bursts causing 429s. POC deadline next Wed, can someone help triage?

maria: @customer-alicia — sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the log-forwarder config and one example request/response (headers + status)? Quick question: are you using the managed log drain or running the sidecar forwarder?

customer-alicia: We're running the sidecar (fluentd) inside our kube cluster. Forwarder config:

```yaml
# forwarding conf (sensitive fields redacted)
<match redwood.logs>
  @type splunk_hec
  host splunk.company.internal
  port 8088
  protocol https
  token REDACTED
  tls true
</match>
```

Also sample HTTP request to Redwood: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-Id: abc123" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://redwood.local/v1/generate`

jonathan: Two quick guesses: 1) Splunk HEC default port is 8088 but your forwarder might be using non-TLS on that port; fluentd splunk plugin complains silently if TLS handshake fails. 2) Trace header mismatch: our runtime expects `x-trace-id` or `traceparent` for distributed traces — `X-Request-Id` isn't automatically mapped.

raj: Also saw 429s in our ingesters when bursts > 5 req/s per connection — sidecar will buffer then drop if drain backpressure is high. Do you have any logs from the redwood sidecar? grep for `rate_limit_exceeded` or `buffer_overflow`.

customer-alicia: Found this in sidecar log: 

```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] error: rate_limit_exceeded service=redwood-ingest retry_after=2.5s req_id=abc123
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] warn: splunk_hec: tls handshake failed host=splunk.company.internal:8088 error="certificate unknown"
```

maria: OK that TLS error explains missing logs. Splunk HEC cert probably isn't trusted by the fluentd runtime. Two immediate options: 1) Configure fluentd to trust the CA (add CA bundle to the sidecar image), or 2) switch to HTTP (non-TLS) over a private network if allowed. Which is easier for you?

customer-alicia: We prefer TLS. How do we add the CA bundle?

jonathan: Mount the CA as a k8s secret and add to the sidecar config via `tls_ca_cert` option in the splunk plugin. Example snippet: `tls true\nca_cert_path /etc/ssl/certs/custom-splunk-ca.pem` and mount secret to that path.

raj: For the 429s: increase `max_buffer_size` on the fluentd buffer and reduce burst concurrency from the POC clients. Also enable exponential backoff on the redwood client side. For an immediate band-aid, set `max_retries` higher so events aren't dropped.

pm-bryan: FYI on traces: we can map `X-Request-Id` to `x-trace-id` at the ingress level while you patch clients. Add this Envoy header transform: `request_header_to_add: { name: "x-trace-id", value: "%REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%" }` — that will make trace IDs visible in the Console and link logs->spans.

customer-alicia: Nice. We'll try CA mount and header transform. One more: how to debug missing trace IDs in Console UI?

maria: On Console: go to Observability -> Traces -> search by service `onprem-sidecar` and filter `trace_id:*`. If you see spans but no trace IDs, it's because the runtime emitted synthetic ids (we use `trace_id` only if propagated). Also check the ingestion JSON for `trace_id` field.

customer-alicia: I grep'd an ingest file and saw entries like: "trace_id": null for some requests.

jonathan: That matches header problem. After you add the Envoy transform and restart clients, new events should show `trace_id` present. For older events we can't retroactively inject.

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy alert: redwood-sidecar/namespace-prod had 37% packet drops in last 5m — investigate if still happening.

raj: One more gotcha we saw in on‑prem POCs: Splunk HEC tokens sometimes have per-token rate caps on ingestion. If your Splunk team applied a token-level throttle, the sidecar will get 429s even if Redwood accepted events. Ask Splunk ops to check token throttling and backpressure metrics.

customer-alicia: Good call — pinged Splunk ops. They replied token has 5k events/min limit and we're spiking during load tests.

maria: Ok plan of action summarized: 1) Mount Splunk CA into fluentd and set `ca_cert_path` (fix TLS) 2) Add Envoy header transform to map `X-Request-Id` -> `x-trace-id` (fix traces) 3) Tune fluentd buffer/retries and coordinate token limits with Splunk ops (fix 429s/drop) 4) If needed, enable Redwood's managed log-forwarder temporarily to bypass sidecar.

customer-alicia: I'll try 1–3 now, can we get a quick pairing session if we hit issues? Maybe 30m with eng oncall?

maria: Yep — I booked a 30m slot with @jonathan and @raj at 15:30 PT. Invite sent. :thumbsup:

customer-alicia: Thanks all — I'll report back after the pairing.

pm-bryan: Also added a temporary Canary route in Console that will stream logs to a debug endpoint so you can watch ingestion in near-real-time: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/streams/canary123 (only valid for the POC org)

customer-alicia: Seeing logs in the canary stream now after CA fix, and trace_id populated after header transform. 429s reduced after Splunk increased token cap. :tada:

maria: Awesome — closing the loop. If you want, we can add a short runbook with the fluentd CA mount + Envoy header snippet for your infra repo.

customer-alicia: Yes please, that would be great.

jonathan: Will draft the runbook and paste here by EOD.

customer-alicia: Thanks everyone!"
